Peanut Brittle is something I remember my mom making every holiday season, I always loved the stuff (and have a Massive sweet tooth) so I started making it myself probably a decade ago. Ran through several recipes before settling on this one and it's a major hit with my in-law family. Actually, it's a hit with lots of people as I've sold it a couple of years for $8/pound and was delivering 20~30lbs most days between T-giving and X-mas. This year I got sick a few days after Thanksgiving and am only just finally getting over it now, so I'm a bit behind on doling out the X-mas gifts.... but, better late than never. :)

Peanut Brittle

Ingredients

 2 cups white sugar (16 ounce)
 1 cup light corn syrup (8 ounce)
 1/2 teaspoon salt (0.2 ounce)
 1/2 cup water
 2 cups dry-roasted peanuts (9 ounces)
 1/4 cup butter, softened
 2 teaspoons baking soda

Instructions

 In a heavy saucepan, over medium heat, bring to a boil sugar, corn syrup, salt, and water. Stir until sugar is dissolved. 
 Heat to 280 degrees F, then stir in peanuts. Set candy thermometer in place, and continue cooking. 
 Stir frequently until temperature reaches 300 degrees F.
 
 Remove from heat; immediately stir in butter and baking soda; pour at once onto table. 
 Smooth out with wooden spoon; cool. Snap candy into pieces.

I will scale this up 3 times in a 10qt pot, you Absolutely need headspace as when you stir in the baking soda it will foam up. I also have a stainless steel prep table which is where I pour it to cool. Make sure that your surface is WELL greased so the candy will release. I use spray oil, if you go this route make Absolutely certain that it doesn't list water as an ingredient (else the whole batch of candy will stick fast). In the winter, with my house at 64F, it takes 50 minutes for the candy to cool enough to break and package.

Once you add the peanuts you'll need to stir every few seconds else they will burn on the bottom, not tasty. I also use high heat exclusively, everything happens faster but there's no real reason not to.... just cut the burner off (if electric) at 295 and the candy will coast to over 300F.

It's best to do this on low humidity days and you Absolutely want to store this in an airtight container. Don't stick it in the fridge either (it's a humid environment)... I use food-safe desiccant packs, but bought something like 5000 of them back when I was selling this stuff, along with those coffee bags.

Absolutely a great treat and very easy to make for a candy. It's lite and very brittle/crunchy with good butter flavor.
